# Preview OTel Java agent 3.0 in Splunk with one flag

The OpenTelemetry Java agent 3.0 is close, and the project asks users to preview it with one environment variable,
`OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true`. This lab turns it on for a running Java system on EKS and shows, in
Splunk Observability Cloud, what changes: the connection pool metric names, the unit of the pool timings, and the
database keys on real traces.

## What runs

- EKS with two t3.large nodes (`main.tf`), the Splunk OTel Collector (Helm chart 0.163.1).
- Two Spring Boot services, `orders` and `inventory`, on Postgres. The jar is built once in the cluster.
- The OTel Java agent 2.33.1, attached through `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`.

`reproduce.sh` runs the agent with its defaults and a fixed load of one order every 50 ms for 120 seconds, then reads
from Splunk: the database metric names, the pool series under `db.client.connections.*` for each service, the
`db.client.operation.duration` series, and every database key=value pair on one trace through Splunk's trace API.

`fix.sh` starts a preview pair, `orders-v3` and `inventory-v3`, next to the default pair on the same node. It uses the same
jar, image, Collector and agent options, with `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true` added. The only other
difference is `deployment.environment`, which gets a `-v3` suffix so Splunk keeps the pairs apart. Three rounds of the
same load (90 seconds, the first 30 as warm-up) hit both pairs at the same time. Each round gives one stored mean of the
connection use time from each pair over the same minutes, and the script requires every round's ratio to fall between
500 and 2000, since the same timing stored in milliseconds and in seconds should differ by about 1000.

`check.sh` is a free check with Docker and console exporters: it proves the same name and unit change before any cloud run.

## Run it yourself

You need an AWS account, Terraform, kubectl, Helm, jq and a Splunk Observability Cloud org with an ingest token and an API token.

```bash
export AWS_REGION=eu-central-1 LAB_NAME=agent3-preview-$RANDOM
export SPLUNK_REALM=us1 SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=... SPLUNK_API_TOKEN=...
terraform init && terraform apply -var region=$AWS_REGION -var lab_name=$LAB_NAME
./reproduce.sh && ./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh && terraform destroy -var region=$AWS_REGION -var lab_name=$LAB_NAME
```

Each script finishes within 14 minutes, waits included. The EKS control plane takes about 10 minutes to create.

## What the run shows

The names and keys each mode sends are printed in the run's log, read back from Splunk: the pool metric names, the
stored use time per round, and every database key on one trace from each pair. Use those lists, not this README, as the
record of what changed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, run on a GitHub runner with Docker before AWS is paid for. It uses the lab's own source, images, agent
# and load script, and proves that OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true alone moves the agent's database span
# keys and connection pool metrics to the new names, with pool timings in seconds. Kubernetes and Splunk are tested by
# the rehearsal. No secrets are used here.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/src c/out c/init c/load

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
open("c/src/pom.xml", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "pom.xml"))
open("c/src/App.java", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "App.java"))
open("c/init/init.sql", "w").write(block("k8s/10-app.yaml", "init.sql"))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY

IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'maven:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
PY_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ ]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
PG_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'postgres:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
AGENT_URL=$(grep -m1 -oE 'https://github.com/[^"]+\.jar' k8s/00-build.yaml)
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== Fetching the agent and building the jar"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$PY_IMAGE" python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlretrieve('$AGENT_URL', '/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar')" && break
  sleep 10
done
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  set -e; mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab; cp /src/pom.xml /w/; cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/; cd /w
  mvn -q -B -DskipTests package; cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar'
ls -l c/out

docker run -d --name postgres --network lab -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=lab -v "$PWD/c/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro" "$PG_IMAGE" -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
sleep 3

start() {   # name, then any extra docker arguments. The agent options are the same in both runs.
  local name=$1; shift
  docker run -d --name "$name" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab:ro" --entrypoint java "$@" \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=postgres \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=lab -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8080 \
    -e "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$name -Dotel.traces.exporter=console -Dotel.metrics.exporter=console -Dotel.metric.export.interval=5000 -Dotel.logs.exporter=none" \
    "$IMAGE" -Xms256m -Xmx256m -jar /lab/app.jar >/dev/null
}
ready() {
  for i in $(seq 1 90); do docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -oE 'process running for [0-9.]+' | tail -1 | sed "s/^/$1 /"
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' || { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1; }
}
load() { docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e SECONDS_TOTAL=20 -e SECONDS_WARM=5 "$PY_IMAGE" python /load/load.py; }
db_names() { grep -oE 'name=db\.[a-z._]+' "$1" | sed 's/name=//' | sort -u || true; }
pool_names() { db_names "$1" | grep -E "^$2\." || true; }
unit_of() { grep -oE "name=$2, description=[^,]*, unit=[a-z]+" "$1" | head -1 | grep -oE 'unit=[a-z]+$' | cut -d= -f2 || true; }
span_keys() { grep LoggingSpanExporter "$1" | grep -E ' CLIENT .*db\.' | tail -1 | grep -oE '\bdb\.[a-z_.]+=' | tr -d = | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '; echo; }

run() {   # name, then any extra docker arguments for both services
  local name=$1; shift
  docker rm -f orders inventory >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  start inventory "$@"
  start orders "$@"
  ready inventory
  ready orders
  load | tee "c/$name.txt"
  grep -q 'errors=0' "c/$name.txt" || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: requests failed in the $name run"; exit 1; }
  sleep 8
  { docker logs orders 2>&1; docker logs inventory 2>&1; } > "c/$name.log"
  echo "-- $name run: database metric names"
  db_names "c/$name.log" | sed 's/^/  /'
  echo "-- $name run: database span keys: $(span_keys "c/$name.log")"
}

echo "== The agent with its defaults"
run default
grep -m1 -h 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' c/default.log || true
echo "== The same agent options, with OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true"
run preview -e OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true

D_OLD=$(pool_names c/default.log db.client.connections | grep -c . || true)
D_NEW=$(pool_names c/default.log db.client.connection | grep -c . || true)
P_OLD=$(pool_names c/preview.log db.client.connections | grep -c . || true)
P_NEW=$(pool_names c/preview.log db.client.connection | grep -c . || true)
D_UNIT=$(unit_of c/default.log db.client.connections.use_time)
P_UNIT=$(unit_of c/preview.log db.client.connection.use_time)
D_KEYS=$(span_keys c/default.log)
P_KEYS=$(span_keys c/preview.log)
echo "pool names: default old $D_OLD new $D_NEW, preview old $P_OLD new $P_NEW"
echo "use_time unit: default ${D_UNIT:-none}, preview ${P_UNIT:-none}"
echo "span keys: default [$D_KEYS] preview [$P_KEYS]"
[ "$D_OLD" -ge 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the default run has no pool metric under db.client.connections"; exit 1; }
[ "$D_NEW" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the default run already uses the new pool names"; exit 1; }
[ "$P_NEW" -ge 1 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the preview run has no pool metric under db.client.connection"; exit 1; }
[ "$P_OLD" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the preview run still sends old pool names"; exit 1; }
[ "$D_UNIT" = ms ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the default use_time unit is not ms"; exit 1; }
[ "$P_UNIT" = s ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the preview use_time unit is not s"; exit 1; }
[[ " $D_KEYS " == *" db.system "* ]] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the default span has no db.system"; exit 1; }
[[ " $P_KEYS " == *" db.system.name "* ]] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the preview span has no db.system.name"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AFTER: a preview pair (orders-v3, inventory-v3) starts next to the default pair on the same node: same jar, image,
# Collector and agent options, plus OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true and its own deployment.environment.
# Three rounds of the same load hit both pairs at once, so each round gives one reading per mode over the same minutes.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=830
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; type diagnose >/dev/null 2>&1 && diagnose; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_fixed"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] && [ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "the Splunk settings are not set"
source ./lib.sh
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"
newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }

echo "== 1. Starting the preview pair next to the default pair: one environment variable added"
for s in inventory orders; do
  kubectl -n demo get deploy "$s" -o json | jq --arg s "$s" --arg d "$DEFAULT_ENV" --arg p "$PREVIEW_ENV" '
    {apiVersion, kind, metadata: {name: "\($s)-v3", namespace: "demo"},
     spec: (.spec | .selector.matchLabels.app = "\($s)-v3" | .template.metadata.labels.app = "\($s)-v3"
       | .template.spec.containers[0].env |= (map(
           if .name == "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS" then .value |= sub("deployment.environment=" + $d; "deployment.environment=" + $p)
           elif .name == "INVENTORY_URL" then .value = "http://inventory-v3:8080" else . end)
         + [{name: "OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW", value: "true"}]))}' | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not create $s-v3"
  kubectl -n demo expose deploy "$s-v3" --port 8080 --target-port 8080 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory-v3 --timeout="$(cap 150 600)s" >/dev/null || fail "inventory-v3 did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders-v3 --timeout="$(cap 150 600)s" >/dev/null || fail "orders-v3 did not start"
for s in orders inventory orders-v3 inventory-v3; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s: node $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}'), jar $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}')"
  kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name == "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS" or (.name | startswith("OTEL_"))) | "  \(.name)=\(.value)"'
  [ "$(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}')" = "$(cat jar-sha.txt)" ] || fail "$s runs a different jar"
done
echo "same jar in all four pods: yes"

echo "== 2. Three rounds: the same load on both pairs at the same time, 90 seconds each, the first 30 as warm-up"
warm_preview
: > rounds.txt
for r in 1 2 3; do
  kubectl -n demo delete pod "load-d$r" "load-v$r" --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  load_pod "load-d$r" orders || fail "could not start round $r for the default pair"
  load_pod "load-v$r" orders-v3 || fail "could not start round $r for the preview pair"
  for p in "load-d$r" "load-v$r"; do
    kubectl -n demo wait "pod/$p" --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 130 200)s" >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs "$p" --tail=10; fail "round $r: $p did not finish"; }
  done
  end=$(date +%s)
  for p in "load-d$r" "load-v$r"; do kubectl -n demo logs "$p" > "$p.txt"; grep -E 'target=|requests=' "$p.txt" | sed "s/^/  round $r $p: /"; done
  start=$(grep -oE 'started_epoch=[0-9]+' "load-d$r.txt" | cut -d= -f2)
  echo "$r $start $end" >> rounds.txt
  [ "$r" -lt 3 ] && sleep 60   # a quiet minute, so each round's window holds only that round
done

load_counts
source ./load.env
rate_gap=$(awk -v a="$default_rps" -v b="$preview_rps" 'BEGIN{d = (a - b) / b * 100; printf "%.1f", (d < 0 ? -d : d)}')
echo "the two pairs' rates differ by ${rate_gap}%"
[ "$default_errors" -eq 0 ] && [ "$preview_errors" -eq 0 ] || fail "requests failed during the rounds"
# The same load means rates within 5% of each other and near the 20 per second target. The Postgres lab reached 19.1
# per second for one pair on this node, so the floor is 18.
awk -v g="$rate_gap" -v a="$default_rps" -v b="$preview_rps" 'BEGIN{ exit !(g <= 5 && a >= 18 && a <= 21 && b >= 18 && b <= 21) }' \
  || fail "the pairs did not get the same load: $default_rps and $preview_rps per second, ${rate_gap}% apart"

echo "== 3. What Splunk Observability Cloud stores for each pair"
pool=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 150 300)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  pool=$(pool_series "$PREVIEW_ENV" "$NEW_POOL" inventory)
  echo "  t+$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s: preview pool series under $NEW_POOL.* for inventory: ${pool:-0}"
  [ "${pool:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 20
done
[ "${pool:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no pool metric under the new names reached Splunk"
sleep 75   # the last round's minute closes up to 60 s after it ends, then Splunk needs time
echo "-- database metric names in Splunk with the agent's defaults"
names_in "$DEFAULT_ENV" | tee names-default.txt | sed 's/^/  /'
echo "-- database metric names in Splunk with the 3.0 preview"
names_in "$PREVIEW_ENV" | tee names-preview.txt | sed 's/^/  /'
echo "-- names in only one mode"
comm -3 names-default.txt names-preview.txt | sed 's/^\t/  preview only: /; t; s/^/  default only: /'
new_min=999; legacy_total=0
for s in orders inventory; do
  n=$(pool_series "$PREVIEW_ENV" "$NEW_POOL" "$s"); l=$(pool_series "$PREVIEW_ENV" "$LEGACY_POOL" "$s")
  echo "preview, $s: pool series under $NEW_POOL.* ${n:-0}, under $LEGACY_POOL.* ${l:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: preview_new_pool_series[$s]=${n:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: preview_legacy_pool_series[$s]=${l:-0}"
  [ "${n:-0}" -lt "$new_min" ] && new_min=${n:-0}
  legacy_total=$(( legacy_total + ${l:-0} ))
done
ops=$(op_series "$PREVIEW_ENV")
echo "preview: db.client.operation.duration series $ops"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: operation_duration_series[preview]=${ops:-0}"

echo "-- the same pool timing per round, read for both pairs over the same minutes"
ratios_ok=1; ratio_max=0
while read -r r s e; do
  from_ms=$(( s * 1000 )); to_ms=$(( (e + 59) * 1000 ))
  dm=$(use_time_mean "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$LEGACY_POOL" "$from_ms" "$to_ms")
  pm=$(use_time_mean "$PREVIEW_ENV" "$NEW_POOL" "$from_ms" "$to_ms")
  [ -n "$dm" ] && [ -n "$pm" ] || { echo "round $r: a mean could not be read (default '${dm}', preview '${pm}')"; ratios_ok=0; continue; }
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$dm" -v b="$pm" 'BEGIN{ if (b > 0) printf "%.1f", a / b }')
  echo "round $r: default $dm (stored in ms), preview $pm (stored in s), ratio ${ratio:-none}"
  echo "stored use time, round $r: default $dm"
  echo "stored use time, round $r: preview $pm"
  [ -n "$ratio" ] && echo "HERO_MEASURE: use_time_ratio[round_$r]=$ratio"
  ratio_max=$(awk -v x="${ratio:-0}" -v m="$ratio_max" 'BEGIN{ print (x > m ? x : m) }')
  awk -v x="${ratio:-0}" 'BEGIN{ exit !(x >= 500 && x <= 2000) }' || ratios_ok=0
done < rounds.txt
echo "HERO_MEASURE: use_time_ratio_max=$ratio_max"
echo "every ratio within 500 to 2000: $([ "$ratios_ok" = 1 ] && echo yes || echo no)"

echo "-- database spans on one trace per pair, from Splunk APM"
dt=$(grep -oE 'last_trace_id=[0-9a-f]+' load-d3.txt | cut -d= -f2)
pt=$(grep -oE 'last_trace_id=[0-9a-f]+' load-v3.txt | cut -d= -f2)
fetch_trace "$dt" trace-default-round3.json || echo "  trace $dt: no database spans yet"
fetch_trace "$pt" trace-preview-round3.json || echo "  trace $pt: no database spans yet"
echo "default pair, trace $dt:"; db_spans trace-default-round3.json | sed 's/^/  /'
echo "preview pair, trace $pt:"; db_spans trace-preview-round3.json | sed 's/^/  /'
dk=$(db_keys trace-default-round3.json); pk=$(db_keys trace-preview-round3.json)
echo "database span keys, default: ${dk:-none found}"
echo "database span keys, preview: ${pk:-none found}"
p_old=$(count_in "$pk" "$LEGACY_KEYS"); p_new=$(count_in "$pk" "$NEW_KEYS"); p_svc=$(db_services trace-preview-round3.json)
echo "preview keys: old $p_old, new $p_new, from $p_svc services"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: span_db_keys[preview_old]=$p_old"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: span_db_keys[preview_new]=$p_new"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: preview_old_span_keys=$p_old"

[ "$new_min" -ge 1 ] && [ "$legacy_total" -eq 0 ] && [ "$p_new" -ge 1 ] && [ "$p_old" -eq 0 ] && [ "$p_svc" -ge 2 ] && [ "$ratios_ok" = 1 ] \
  || { echo "the preview pair did not show only new names from both services, or a ratio left 500 to 2000"; emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
emit fixed

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: db-init
  namespace: demo
data:
  init.sql: |
    create extension pg_stat_statements;
    create table stock (id int primary key, sku text not null, qty int not null);
    insert into stock select i, 'SKU-' || i, 100 + i from generate_series(1, 100) i;
    create table reserved (id int primary key, qty int not null);
    insert into reserved select i, i % 7 from generate_series(1, 100) i;
    create table audit (id int primary key);
    insert into audit select i from generate_series(1, 10) i;
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: postgres }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: postgres }
    spec:
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: init
          configMap:
            name: db-init
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16.4-alpine
          args: ["-c", "shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements"]
          env:
            - { name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD, value: lab }
          ports:
            - containerPort: 5432
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: init, mountPath: /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d }
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command: ["pg_isready", "-U", "postgres"]
            periodSeconds: 3
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
  namespace: demo
spec:
  selector: { app: postgres }
  ports:
    - port: 5432
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: orders
  namespace: demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: orders }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: orders }
    spec:
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      volumes:
        - name: lab
          hostPath: { path: /opt/lab }
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-21
          command: ["java", "-Xms256m", "-Xmx256m", "-jar", "/lab/app.jar"]
          env:
            - name: HOST_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef: { fieldPath: status.hostIP }
            - { name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL, value: "jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres" }
            - { name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME, value: postgres }
            - { name: SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD, value: lab }
            - { name: INVENTORY_URL, value: "http://inventory:8080" }
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: lab, mountPath: /lab, readOnly: true }
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 512Mi }
            limits: { memory: 1Gi }
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: 8080 }
            periodSeconds: 2

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Aims for one order request every 50 ms to TARGET (orders by default) in every run, and fix.sh reports the rate reached.
    import http.client, os, random, sys, time
    seconds, warm = int(os.environ["SECONDS_TOTAL"]), int(os.environ["SECONDS_WARM"])
    target = os.environ.get("TARGET", "orders")
    conn, took, errors, last, gap = http.client.HTTPConnection(target, 8080, timeout=10), [], 0, "", 0.05
    minutes = {}
    start = time.time()
    print("LOAD target=%s started_epoch=%d" % (target, start), flush=True)
    while time.time() - start < seconds:
        sent = time.time()
        minutes[int(sent // 60) * 60] = minutes.get(int(sent // 60) * 60, 0) + 1
        last = "%032x" % random.getrandbits(128)
        try:
            conn.request("GET", "/orders/%d" % random.randint(1, 1000), headers={"traceparent": "00-%s-%016x-01" % (last, random.getrandbits(64))})
            r = conn.getresponse(); r.read()
            ok = r.status == 200
        except Exception:
            ok = False
            conn.close()
        ms = (time.time() - sent) * 1000
        if not ok:
            errors += 1
        elif sent - start >= warm:
            took.append(ms)
        time.sleep(max(0, gap - ms / 1000))
    for minute in sorted(minutes):
        print("LOAD minute=%d sent=%d" % (minute, minutes[minute]))
    took.sort()
    if not took:
        print("LOAD no successful requests after warm-up, errors=%d" % errors)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("LOAD requests=%d errors=%d p50_ms=%.2f p95_ms=%.2f" % (len(took), errors, took[len(took) // 2], took[int(len(took) * 0.95)]))
    print("LOAD last_trace_id=%s" % last)
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  volumes:
    - name: load
      configMap:
        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: SECONDS_TOTAL, value: "540" }
        - { name: SECONDS_WARM, value: "30" }
        - { name: TARGET, value: "orders" }
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: load, mountPath: /load }

# The readings behind reproduce.sh and fix.sh: Splunk reads, the trace read, the load pods and small arithmetic.
# Sourced, never run alone. Every SignalFlow program sent is appended to signalflow-programs.txt and printed.
# The default pair (orders, inventory) sends deployment.environment=$DEFAULT_ENV. The preview pair (orders-v3,
# inventory-v3) runs the same jar and image with OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_COMMON_V3_PREVIEW=true and sends $PREVIEW_ENV.
# Both pairs report service names orders and inventory, so every read here filters on the environment.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
DEFAULT_ENV="${LAB_NAME}"
PREVIEW_ENV="${LAB_NAME}-v3"
LEGACY_POOL="db.client.connections"     # the 2.x names, as the agent sends them with its defaults
NEW_POOL="db.client.connection"         # the stable names the 3.0 preview sends
# Keys the free check saw on the agent's database spans: the default run, then the preview run.
LEGACY_KEYS="db.connection_string db.name db.operation db.sql.table db.statement db.system db.user"
NEW_KEYS="db.namespace db.query.summary db.query.text db.system.name db.operation.name db.collection.name"

series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

# The metric names exactly as Splunk stores them, for one environment.
names_in() { series "sf_metric:db.* AND deployment.environment:$1" | jq -r '[.results[]?.metric // empty] | unique | .[]' 2>/dev/null; }

# Pool series under one name family for one environment and service. The trailing dot keeps db.client.connection.
# from also matching db.client.connections.
pool_series() {   # environment, family, service
  series "sf_metric:$2.* AND deployment.environment:$1 AND service.name:$3" | jq --arg f "$2." '[.results[]? | select(.metric | startswith($f))] | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

op_series() { series "sf_metric:db.client.operation.duration* AND deployment.environment:$1" | jq '.results | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=60000&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs <= $to) | [.data[]?.value // empty] | add // empty' 2>/dev/null
}

# The mean connection use time as Splunk stores it, over one window: the sum divided by the count, across both services.
# No unit conversion happens here, so the old metric reads in milliseconds and the new one in seconds.
use_time_mean() {   # environment, family, start ms, stop ms
  local f="filter('deployment.environment', '$1')" s c
  local ps="data('$2.use_time_sum', filter=$f, rollup='delta').sum().publish('s')"
  local pc="data('$2.use_time_count', filter=$f, rollup='delta').sum().publish('c')"
  printf '%s\n%s\n' "$ps" "$pc" | tee -a signalflow-programs.txt | sed 's/^/  program: /' >&2
  local try
  for try in 1 2 3; do   # a stream can come back empty once, so a sum or count of zero is read again
    s=$(signalflow "$ps" "$3" "$4" | awk '{t += $1} END {printf "%.6f", t}')
    c=$(signalflow "$pc" "$3" "$4" | awk '{t += $1} END {printf "%.0f", t}')
    awk -v s="$s" -v c="$c" 'BEGIN{ exit !(s > 0 && c > 0) }' && break
    echo "  read $try gave sum $s over $c uses; reading again" >&2; sleep 5
  done
  echo "  $2.use_time in $1 from $(( $3 / 1000 )) to $(( $4 / 1000 )): sum $s over $c uses" >&2
  awk -v s="$s" -v c="$c" 'BEGIN { if (c > 0) printf "%.6f", s / c; else print "" }'
}

# The trace as Splunk APM returns it. Splunk can take a minute or two to index a trace, so this asks again for up to
# about three minutes, and keeps the raw reply in the lab directory.
fetch_trace() {   # trace id, file
  local i
  for i in $(seq 1 12); do
    curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" -o "$2" 2>/dev/null
    [ -n "$(db_keys "$2")" ] && return 0
    sleep 15
  done
  return 1
}

# Every database span's key=value pairs, sorted, one line per span. Tags can come as an object or as key/value pairs.
db_spans() {
  jq -r '.. | objects | select(has("tags")) | . as $s
    | (.tags | if type == "object" then to_entries elif type == "array" then map({key: .key, value: .value}) else [] end
       | map(select(.key | startswith("db.")))) as $t
    | select($t | length > 0)
    | "\($s.serviceName // $s.service // "?") \($s.operationName // $s.name // "?"): \($t | sort_by(.key) | map("\(.key)=\(.value | tostring)") | join(" "))"' "$1" 2>/dev/null | sort -u
}

# How many services have database spans on a trace, from db_spans' first word.
db_services() { db_spans "$1" | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u | grep -c . || true; }

db_keys() { db_spans "$1" | sed 's/^[^:]*: //' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/=.*//' | grep '^db\.' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//'; }

count_in() {   # space-separated keys found, space-separated keys to count
  local n=0 k
  for k in $2; do [[ " $1 " == *" $k "* ]] && n=$(( n + 1 )); done
  echo "$n"
}

# What a failed run needs to explain itself: the agent's export errors, the Collector's logs and what Splunk holds.
diagnose() {
  local s pod
  echo "-- diagnostics: agent export errors"
  for s in orders inventory orders-v3 inventory-v3; do
    kubectl -n demo logs "deploy/$s" -c app --tail=2000 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'failed to export|exporter.*(error|fail)|connection refused|\bERROR\b' | tail -4 | cut -c1-200 | sed "s/^/  $s: /"
  done
  for pod in $(kubectl -n splunk get pods -l component=otel-collector-agent -o name 2>/dev/null | sed 's|pod/||'); do
    kubectl -n splunk logs "$pod" --tail=500 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'error|dropp|refused|unauthorized|forbidden' | tail -5 | cut -c1-220 | sed "s/^/  collector $pod: /"
  done
  for e in "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$PREVIEW_ENV"; do
    echo "-- database metric names in Splunk for $e"
    names_in "$e" | sed 's/^/  /'
  done
}

# One load pod for one pair. The load script's ConfigMap is already in place from reproduce.sh.
load_pod() {   # pod name, target service
  awk 'f; /^---$/ { f = 1 }' k8s/20-load.yaml |
    sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e 's/value: "540"/value: "90"/' -e "s/^  name: load\$/  name: $1/" \
        -e "s/{ name: TARGET, value: \"orders\" }/{ name: TARGET, value: \"$2\" }/" | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
}

# Failed requests and the rate reached per pair, over the three rounds. A missing count is a failed read, never a zero.
# Writes default_rps, preview_rps, default_errors and preview_errors to load.env.
load_counts() {
  local mode r e n errs sent name rps
  : > load.env
  for mode in d v; do
    errs=0; sent=0
    for r in 1 2 3; do
      e=$(grep -oE 'errors=[0-9]+' "load-$mode$r.txt" | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)
      n=$(grep -oE 'requests=[0-9]+' "load-$mode$r.txt" | cut -d= -f2)
      [ -n "$e" ] && [ -n "$n" ] || fail "round $r: load-$mode$r printed no counts"
      errs=$(( errs + e )); sent=$(( sent + n ))
    done
    name=$([ "$mode" = d ] && echo default || echo preview)
    rps=$(awk -v n="$sent" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", n / 180}')
    echo "$name: failed requests $errs, requests after warm-up $sent over 3 x 60 s, $rps per second (target 20)"
    echo "HERO_MEASURE: load_errors[$name]=$errs"
    echo "HERO_MEASURE: achieved_rps[$name]=$rps"
    printf '%s_rps=%s\n%s_errors=%s\n' "$name" "$rps" "$name" "$errs" >> load.env
  done
}

# A new counter has no earlier point to take a delta from, so the preview pair gets one unmeasured 90-second load before
# round 1, the way the default pair was already warmed by reproduce.sh. Nothing from it is read.
warm_preview() {
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load-warm --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  load_pod load-warm orders-v3 || fail "could not start the warm-up load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load-warm --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 130 400)s" >/dev/null || fail "the warm-up load did not finish"
  echo "warm-up on the preview pair: $(kubectl -n demo logs load-warm | grep -oE 'requests=[0-9]+ errors=[0-9]+')"
  sleep 30
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: orders calls inventory, which reads Postgres, on EKS with the Splunk OTel Collector and the OTel Java agent
# 2.33.1 on its defaults. Records what Splunk stores: pool metric names per service, db.client.operation.duration and
# every database key on a real trace. fix.sh then runs the preview pair beside this one.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=810
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; type diagnose >/dev/null 2>&1 && diagnose; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_reproduced"; }' EXIT

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o wide || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# The app stays on one node and the load generator on the other, in both runs.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] && [ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] && [ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "the Splunk settings are not set"
source ./lib.sh
newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
echo "environments, new each run: default $DEFAULT_ENV, preview $PREVIEW_ENV"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1), the same in both runs"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"

echo "== 3. Building the jar in the cluster, once, and fetching the agent"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
state=""
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 430 300)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  state=$(kubectl -n demo get job build -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null)
  case "$state" in *Complete*|*Failed*) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build --all-containers --tail=5 2>/dev/null || true
case "$state" in *Complete*) ;; *) kubectl -n demo describe job build | tail -15; fail "the build did not finish: ${state:-still running}" ;; esac
echo "build: $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying Postgres, orders and inventory"
sed "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the app"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/postgres --timeout="$(cap 90 200)s" || fail "postgres did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 180)s" || fail "inventory did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" || fail "orders did not start"

echo "== 5. Attaching the agent with its defaults: no preview flag, no opt-in"
for s in orders inventory; do
  kubectl -n demo set env "deployment/$s" "JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-javaagent:/lab/opentelemetry-javaagent.jar -Dotel.service.name=$s -Dotel.exporter.otlp.endpoint=http://\$(HOST_IP):4318 -Dotel.resource.attributes=deployment.environment=$DEFAULT_ENV -Dotel.logs.exporter=none" >/dev/null || fail "could not attach the agent to $s"
done
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" >/dev/null || fail "inventory did not roll out"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 170)s" >/dev/null || fail "orders did not roll out"
for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s jar: $(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar)"
  echo "$s OTEL_ variables on the pod: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq -r '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(startswith("OTEL_"))] | if length == 0 then "none" else join(" ") end')"
  kubectl -n demo logs "$p" -c app 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 'opentelemetry-javaagent - version' | sed "s/^/$s /"
done
kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest orders)" -c app -- sha256sum /lab/app.jar | awk '{print $1}' > jar-sha.txt

echo "== 6. A fixed load: one order every 50 ms for 120 seconds"
kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e 's/value: "540"/value: "120"/' k8s/20-load.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout="$(cap 160 15)s" || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=20; fail "the load did not finish"; }
LOAD_END=$(date +%s)
kubectl -n demo logs load | tee load-before.txt
errors=$(grep -oE 'errors=[0-9]+' load-before.txt | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2)
echo "failed requests in the default run's first load: ${errors:-missing}"
[ -n "$errors" ] || fail "the load printed no error count, so this run can't be used"
[ "$errors" -eq 0 ] || fail "the load saw errors, so this run can't be used"
load_start=$(grep -oE 'started_epoch=[0-9]+' load-before.txt | cut -d= -f2)
trace=$(grep -oE 'last_trace_id=[0-9a-f]+' load-before.txt | cut -d= -f2)
printf 'from_ms=%s\nto_ms=%s\n' "$(( load_start * 1000 ))" "$(( (LOAD_END + 120) * 1000 ))" > window-default.env

echo "== 7. What Splunk Observability Cloud stores for the default environment"
# Splunk's series API lags: wait for this load's pool metric, then one more 60-second export interval.
pool=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 240 240)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  pool=$(pool_series "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$LEGACY_POOL" inventory)
  echo "  t+$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s after the load: pool series under $LEGACY_POOL.*: ${pool:-0}"
  [ "${pool:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 20
done
[ "${pool:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "the pool metric has not reached Splunk"
sleep 60
echo "-- database metric names in Splunk with the agent's defaults"
names_in "$DEFAULT_ENV" | tee names-default.txt | sed 's/^/  /'
legacy_min=999; new_total=0
for s in orders inventory; do
  l=$(pool_series "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$LEGACY_POOL" "$s"); n=$(pool_series "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$NEW_POOL" "$s")
  echo "default run, $s: pool series under $LEGACY_POOL.* ${l:-0}, under $NEW_POOL.* ${n:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: default_pool_series[$s]=${l:-0}"
  [ "${l:-0}" -lt "$legacy_min" ] && legacy_min=${l:-0}
  new_total=$(( new_total + ${n:-0} ))
done
ops=$(op_series "$DEFAULT_ENV")
echo "default run: db.client.operation.duration series $ops"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: operation_duration_series[default]=${ops:-0}"

source ./window-default.env
mean=$(use_time_mean "$DEFAULT_ENV" "$LEGACY_POOL" "$from_ms" "$to_ms")
echo "mean connection use time as stored, default run, first load ($LEGACY_POOL.use_time, milliseconds): ${mean:-none}"

echo "-- every database span on trace $trace, as Splunk APM returns it (raw reply kept in trace-default.json)"
fetch_trace "$trace" trace-default.json || echo "  the trace had no database spans in Splunk yet"
db_spans trace-default.json | sed 's/^/  /'
keys=$(db_keys trace-default.json)
echo "database span keys in Splunk, default run: ${keys:-none found}"
old_k=$(count_in "$keys" "$LEGACY_KEYS"); new_k=$(count_in "$keys" "$NEW_KEYS")
echo "old keys $old_k, new keys $new_k"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: span_db_keys[default_old]=$old_k"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: span_db_keys[default_new]=$new_k"

# The agent sends old keys only (see check.sh); Splunk APM may show new-style keys beside them, so those are reported.
[ "$legacy_min" -ge 1 ] && [ "$new_total" -eq 0 ] && [ "$old_k" -ge 1 ] || { echo "the default run did not show the old pool names and old span keys"; emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
emit reproduced
